questions.q: What planetary rotation causes the daily cycle of day and night on Earth?
options: A) Earth revolving around Sun in 365 days
B) Earth rotating on its axis west-to-east every 24 hours
questions.ans: B) Earth rotating on its axis west-to-east every 24 hours

questions.q: In Odisha, the vocalization (singing) of the _____ bird serves as a traditional bio-indicator announcing coming monsoon rains.
At what time of day does a vertical outdoor stick cast the shortest shadow?

Assertion (A): The Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west every day.
Reason (R): Earth rotates on its axis in the opposite direction, from west to east.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation.
C) (A) is true, but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.ans: A) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation.

questions.q: How many degrees of longitude rotate past solar light every hour as Earth completes a 360-degree rotation in 24 hours?

sections.section_name: Section B: Short Answer & Reasoning (10 Marks)

questions.q: Give Reason: Shadows cast by trees are long in early morning and late evening, but shortest at noon.
questions.solution: In early morning and evening, the Sun is low on the horizon, striking objects at a sharp slanting angle and casting long shadows. At noon, the Sun is high overhead, casting vertical rays that produce short shadows.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for low Sun slanting angle creating long shadows; 1 Mark for high overhead Sun casting short shadows.

questions.q: How do farmers in Odisha use the song of the Koel bird as an agricultural bio-indicator?
questions.solution: The Koel's singing correlates with seasonal atmospheric shifts marking the arrival of monsoon rains. Hearing the song alerts farmers to time their paddy seed sowing accurately.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for Koel song correlating with monsoon atmospheric shifts; 1 Mark for timing paddy seed sowing.

questions.q: Give Reason: When it is daytime in India, countries on the exact opposite side of Earth (like South America) experience nighttime.
questions.solution: Earth is a spherical globe. As it rotates on its axis relative to the stationary Sun, the sunlit hemisphere facing the Sun experiences day, while the opposite shadowed hemisphere experiences night.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for spherical Earth illuminated on one hemisphere; 1 Mark for opposite shadowed hemisphere experiencing night.

questions.q: Name the five core themes tracked when recording observations in a schoolyard Seasons' Journal.
questions.solution: 1. Plant Life, 2. Birds & Animals, 3. Air, Heat & Light, 4. Water & Water Bodies, 5. Human Lifestyle (clothing/food/farming).
questions.scheme: 2 Marks for listing all 5 core themes correctly (0.4 Mark each).

questions.q: Calculate how many hours of axial rotation take place when Earth rotates through 90 degrees of longitude.
questions.solution:
Earth rotates 15 degrees per hour.
Time = 90 degrees / 15 degrees per hour = 6 hours of axial rotation.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for rotation rate formula (15°/hour); 1 Mark for correct calculation (6 hours).

sections.section_name: Section C: Long Answer, Observation & Application (10 Marks)
sections.question_type: Long Answer / Observation / Diagram / Practical Scenario

questions.q: Describe a classroom globe-and-flashlight simulation experiment to demonstrate Earth's axial rotation and day-night cycle. Detail (a) Apparatus setup, (b) Rotation direction (west to east), (c) Observations for India versus opposite longitudes, and (d) Mathematical calculation of rotation rates.
questions.solution:
1. Setup: Place a globe on a table in a dark room. Shine a stationary flashlight horizontally at the equator representing solar radiation.
2. Rotation Mechanics: Slowly spin the globe counter-clockwise (west to east) on its tilted axis.
3. Observations: When India rotates into the flashlight beam, it experiences sunrise and day, while South America on the shadowed back side experiences night. As rotation continues, India moves into shadow (sunset/night).
4. Rotation Rate Math: 360 degrees / 24 hours = 15 degrees per hour. In 12 hours, 180 degrees rotate past sunlight.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for apparatus setup; 1 Mark for west-to-east rotation direction; 2 Marks for India sunlit vs shadowed observations; 1 Mark for mathematical calculation of 15°/hour.

questions.q: Explain how annual seasonal changes affect (a) Plant life, (b) Animal behavior, (c) Water bodies, and (d) Human lifestyle across Summer, Monsoon, and Winter. Detail how a Seasons' Journal documents these synchronized rhythms.
questions.solution:
1. Seasonal Transformations:
   - Plant Life: Trees shed leaves in dry months, sprout fresh green buds in spring, and bear fruits in summer.
   - Animal Behavior: Birds build nests and incubate eggs in spring; Koel sings before monsoons; migratory birds travel in winter.
   - Water Bodies: Puddles dry up under summer heat, while rivers and ponds overflow during monsoons.
   - Human Lifestyle: People wear cotton in summer and wool in winter, adjusting diets and farming sowing/harvesting cycles.
2. Seasons' Journal Role: Systematic monthly recording across these themes reveals the interconnected rhythms of Earth's biosphere.
questions.scheme: 4 Marks for detailing seasonal impacts across plants, animals, water, and human lifestyle (1 Mark each); 1 Mark for explaining the documentation role of a Seasons' Journal.
